decisions.evidence: Authenticated preimage differs only in explicit initialization admissibility: the R-minimizer must belong to U. Strong convexity gives uniqueness on K but not membership in U (K=[0,1], U=(0,1), R=(x-2)^2). The original instruction already selected such a minimizer; the revision makes its input restriction explicit. Checked the complete current algorithm and its exact protocol, feedback, convexity, gradient and subgradient suppliers. Actual uses in the projection lemma, regret theorem, false-statement witness and both mirror examples meet the condition; no outside direct dependency or reference consumer exists. Dual solvability and projection-in-U remain explicit conditions, not consequences of compactness.

Exact authenticated preimage and current post-reader carrier have identical item bytes; the touched status reflects supporting-record changes. Checked steps 1.1–3.1 against the current OMD definition, current batch-74 OGD procedure, compact Bregman projection lemma and Euclidean definitions. R=||x-x0||^2/2 has gradient x-x0 and Hessian I; expansion gives B_R(x||y)=||x-y||^2/2 for every x0. The dual equation gives y=x_t-eta g and compact strict convexity gives a unique nearest point on K. U=R^d contains initialization and every projection, including boundary minimizers, so the explicit OMD admissibility is met. The statement identifies only the one-step map when eta equals the positive current OGD step; it makes no full-trajectory or degenerate-branch equivalence claim. Thus it does not import the countable-choice hypothesis of the more general unbounded-set OGD projection supplier. Zero g is harmless. No diagram or reader/refuter finding.

Checked steps 1.1–4.1 against the current algorithm, mirror definition, Heine–Borel, lower-semicontinuous extreme-value theorem, convexity and the expanded three-point identity. Continuity on compact nonempty K gives attainment of R and of R minus an affine term; strong convexity gives a strict midpoint contradiction and uniqueness. Only when x_+(y) is in U is its directional derivative used; the feasible segment stays in K and initially in open U even for boundary u. The derivative is nonnegative, making <u-x_+,grad R(y)-grad R(x_+)> nonpositive; the oriented identity then yields the stated inequality. Neither initialization nor projections are claimed automatically to lie in U, so the algorithm restriction is respected. No AC or diagrams; no reader/refuter finding.

Exact authenticated preimage and current post-reader carrier have identical item bytes; the touched status reflects supporting-record changes. Read every step 1.1–6.1, the current algorithm, exact regret/convex/subgradient/Taylor suppliers and the previously independently reviewed Bregman lemmas. Taylor chooses the Hessian for the orientation B_R(y||x), not B_R(x||y). The sum of both orientations is eta<g,x-y>; quadratic completion with A=H(z) proves B_R(x||y)<=eta^2||g||_*^2/2, including zero gradient without division by zero. Projection has the correct oriented Pythagorean sign and all its differentiated points are in U; boundary comparators are permitted by the strong-convexity lower bound. The terminal potential is at x_(T+1) and nonnegative, the initial directional derivative is nonnegative at a constrained minimizer, and finite extrema give the range. Substitution and completion of a square give respectively 3/2 and sqrt(2) constants at the two declared tunings; T=1, coincident iterates and zero gradients cause no exception. Positive D_R and G_R are required only for tuning. Smooth and supplied-supporting-vector cases are both covered; finite choices of Taylor points use no arbitrary AC. The false-statement witness verifies the sharpness claim. The refined algorithm admissibility is already among the theorem hypotheses. No diagrams or reader/refuter finding.
